newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes lower on technical selling.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes lower on technical selling.

text.p: IPE June Brent closed nine cents a barrel lower at $18.52 on Wednesday after a short-lived rally in late trade prompted by players trying to test the upside, traders said.
"There's no fundamentals out there. I think it was technicals that pushed it down...It was a failure to the upside" a broker said.
"Some players tried to test $18.77 but failed," he added.
Less than an hour before the close the contract rallied for a short while, reaching a high of $18.75.
"We're looking very strong, basically we've filled the gap between $18.62 and $18.77. That's the main numbers the locals are looking at," a broker said at the time of the rally.

"We're following heating oil as well this evening, its very, very strong. The spreads haven't changed, they are still -10/-8 (Jun/Jul) and -9/-7 Jul/Aug. But we're mainly looking at the heating oil and this number $18.77," he added.
July Brent closed five cents lower at $18.62.
For most of the day, June Brent maintained a slightly downward slant, trading between one and five cents down. It also touched a low of $18.48 after NYMEX opened.

Earlier, May gas oil settled $3 up at $171.75 at tonne after a late rally on the back of buying interest. The contract touched a high of $172 shortly before the 1630 GMT close. June gas oil also closed higher at $170.50 a tonne, or $2.25 over Tuesday's close.

IPE Brent settled 34 cents higher at $18.61 on Tuesday after supply concerns, technicals and expectations of mildly supportive American Petroleum Institute oil stock data shook it of its earlier lethargy.

The API data issued late on Tuesday showed U.S. distillates stocks fell 1.4 million barrels in the April 25 week. Department of Energy figures issued on Wednesday were in line, showed a drop of 1.6 million barrels over the same period.

API also said that U.S. gasoline stocks fell a modest 408,000 barrels last week while crude stocks rose 1.87 million barrels. The corresponding Energy Department figures were a tiny rise of 100,000 barrels for gasoline and a rise of 2.8 million barrels for crude.
